corrections.previousValue:
Risshaku-ji (山寺) is reached by a direct ≈20-minute Senzan Line train from Yamagata. Admission is {{fact:yamadera-admission-500-yen}}, cash only.

There is no cable car, ropeway, or shortcut anywhere on the mountain — the only way up to the Godaido viewing platform and Okunoin is on foot, via roughly 1,015 stone steps (figures vary 1,015-1,070 depending on the source), and there are no ramps or elevators anywhere on the site, including at the base.

Konponchudo, the main hall about 3 minutes' walk from the base entrance, is a genuinely worthwhile stop on its own without climbing further — the honest option for anyone who'd rather not attempt the stairs.

Lunch: Takifudo Namasoba, near the mountain entrance — ≈50 seats plus a 50-person tatami room, the best-sized option here for a group of 8. Arrive at opening or right after; 10:00-14:00 is when tour groups arrive and the paths and Godaido platform get genuinely crowded, worse still once koyo (autumn foliage) season builds.

Taimenseki, right at the station, is a smaller, quicker soba stop for anyone splitting off from the group lunch or catching an earlier train.

Carry cash for this trip — more than a Tokyo itinerary would need. The Hanagasa Bus to Ginzan Onsen is cash-only (¥1,000/adult, no IC card), and Ginzan Onsen itself has no convenience store or ATM in town (nearest is ≈30 min by car); several ryokan there don't take cards.

Suica/IC coverage thins out fast once you leave central Yamagata city. ⚠ Multiple Japanese sources agree Ōishida Station (the gateway to Ginzan Onsen) doesn't accept IC cards, though this couldn't be confirmed directly against JR East's own site (bot-gated against automated fetch) — buy a paper ticket or plan to pay cash there regardless.

7-Eleven and Japan Post ATMs in Yamagata city itself accept foreign cards normally.
